⚠️ **This card is an instance of a second, unrelated defect — and the evidence is the card itself.**

Two corruptions were applied to this issue between what the seat sent and what GitHub stored, both confirmed by reading the created issue straight back:

**1. The trailing attribution footer was silently dropped.** The body was sent ending with a `---` rule and `_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_`. The stored body ends at *"…no fix is proposed as a diff here."* — rule and footer both gone. ⚠️ Independently observed in the same session on **#15969**, created through the same path, while the identical block **survived verbatim** on a PR body created minutes apart. So it is specific to issue creation, not to the text.

**2. The title's angle-bracket span was eaten.** Sent as ``OS_ALLOW_MAIN_EDITS=1 <cmd>``, stored as ``OS_ALLOW_MAIN_EDITS=1 `` — the `<cmd>` placeholder removed, leaving a trailing space inside the code span. ⚠️ Also previously observed in this session on **#15858**, whose first title spelled a placeholder with angle brackets and came back with the bracketed span eaten, leaving `/projects//…`.

⇒ Two independent observations each, on two different mechanisms. **Titles should spell placeholders as `:id` or `NAME`, never `<…>`.**

## Why this matters beyond tidiness

Every GitHub post from an agent seat is **required** to carry the Claude Code attribution footer. If issue creation strips it silently, then cards filed through that path are non-compliant **and nothing signals it** — the seat believes it posted the footer, and a reader sees a card with no attribution. This seat has filed several cards today through exactly this path.

⛔ Not filed as its own card yet, and deliberately: the mechanism is a harness/tooling behaviour rather than a repository defect, and I have two observations, not a characterisation. Recorded here, on the card that demonstrates it, so the evidence is not lost.

**Durable attribution meanwhile** is the opening prose — *"Filed by the `domain:cli` execution PM seat (#6024)"* — which survives, plus this comment. That is the same workaround the #15733 implementer adopted after hitting it on #15969.

Restating the footer here, since the body lost it:

The sweep the card leaves open is part of the same flight: the Edit/Write sibling's message, the other hooks' env-var hatches (`OS_ALLOW_STASH=1`, the tree-enum guard), and the objectui twins — the pair of repos moves together, as the structural-test flight did today.

p3: no incident, the guard held twice; the hazard is the invitation to route around it, which is why the message is worth one careful flight rather than a shrug. Dispatch when a slot frees; the lane has slots now, so soon.
